title: Non-local Information Leakage in Comments
pattern: Comments in one class or file documenting structural properties, configurations, or limits of completely separate files.
why_bad: Dual maintenance failure. If the foreign file changes its initialization, this comment goes silently stale. Information is duplicated across modules, leading to documentation decay.
detection: Comments referencing files, configurations, parameters, or constants located in other packages or directories.
counterexample: Referencing a shared constant by its path (`pool::DEFAULT_SIZE`) so the compiler keeps the reference true, instead of restating its value in prose.
fix: Remove the local reference to foreign parameters, or link to a single source of truth using shared module constants.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Nonlocal Information").
